findings.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — Caching a device before a successful store update makes a rejected device's next request skip the limit check and authenticate.
pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:110 — The unlocked count-then-upsert lets concurrent new device requests all observe spare capacity and insert past the configured cap.
pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:119 — A client can omit the untrusted device ID header and make tagging return success without ever checking the configured cap.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:49 — Any counting or persistence failure other than the sentinel is logged and authentication succeeds, so database failures silently disable limit enforcement.

packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97 — anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` on GrafanaBootConfig is inferred as type `undefined` while the GrafanaConfig interface declares `number | undefined`, and the constructor's `merge(this, defaults, options)` actually overwrites it with a real server-provided number at runtime, so the concrete class's static type is unsound relative to its own runtime contract.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — tagDeviceUI caches the device key via localCache.SetDefault before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, so once ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned once, subsequent requests from the same device within the 29-minute cache TTL hit the cache and return nil, silently bypassing the device limit and letting anonymous auth succeed without ever persisting/re-checking the device

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:109 — CreateOrUpdateDevice checks CountDevices and then inserts in two separate, non-transactional DB calls, creating a TOCTOU race where concurrent requests near the limit can each pass the count check and all insert, exceeding deviceLimit

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Authenticate() now calls TagDevice synchronously on every anonymous request (was fire-and-forget in a goroutine), so every anon page load blocks on a DB round trip (and a COUNT query when device limit is set) instead of returning immediately

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Removing the goroutine's dedicated 2-minute timeout context means TagDevice now runs under the caller's request context, so a slow/contended DB directly increases latency (or causes failures) for every anonymous authentication request, with no isolation from the auth request path

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — TagDevice now runs synchronously on the request's own ctx with no bounded timeout, so a slow/hung DB blocks every anonymous authentication request instead of the previous fire-and-forget goroutine with a 2-minute timeout that degraded gracefully.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Removing the goroutine's defer recover() means a panic inside TagDevice/tagDeviceUI/CreateOrUpdateDevice now propagates directly out of Authenticate(), risking a crashed/500'd request instead of being safely logged and swallowed as before.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:74 — CreateOrUpdateDevice/updateDevice issue DB calls using the caller-supplied ctx with no per-call timeout applied anywhere in the anon store, so if the underlying DB stalls the query can block for as long as the (possibly unbounded) upstream context allows, whereas before it was capped at 2 minutes.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Anonymous.Authenticate now hard-fails authentication with ErrDeviceLimitReached, which is trivially triggerable by any client sending arbitrary, unsigned X-Grafana-Device-Id header values to exhaust the device cap and deny anonymous access to legitimate users (DoS via unauthenticated request)

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:124 — Device identity used for the new limit/enforcement logic (X-Grafana-Device-Id) is entirely client-supplied and unvalidated/unsigned, so the device count/limit mechanism can be trivially inflated or bypassed by spoofing arbitrary device IDs

pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:198 — AnonymousDeviceLimit is exposed to unauthenticated users via public frontend settings, giving an attacker the exact threshold needed to efficiently exhaust the device cap and trigger the anonymous-auth DoS

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51 — The only limit test stops at the store, so it misses that a failed over-limit tag remains cached and the same device is accepted on retry.
pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:62 — The sequential test misses the non-atomic count-then-insert race that lets concurrent first-time devices exceed the configured cap.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:69 — The test never verifies that an existing active device can still be refreshed at capacity, leaving the new update-only success branch untested.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Authenticate() changed from async fire-and-forget to synchronous with ErrDeviceLimitReached now failing anonymous auth, but there is no client_test.go at all exercising Authenticate, so this behavioral change has zero test coverage

goldens.comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — Caching a device before a successful store update makes a rejected device's next request skip the limit check and authenticate.
pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:110 — The unlocked count-then-upsert lets concurrent new device requests all observe spare capacity and insert past the configured cap.
pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:119 — A client can omit the untrusted device ID header and make tagging return success without ever checking the configured cap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a device-limit check inside `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` (counting recent devices and returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when an update affects 0 rows) and propagates errors from `TagDevice`/`tagDeviceUI` (`impl.go` now `return err`). However, the diff does not show any logic about an "untrusted device ID header" being optional, nor any branch where tagging returns success specifically when that header is omitted. Since the referenced header-handling behavior is not present in the provided hunks, the claim cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:49 — Any counting or persistence failure other than the sentinel is logged and authentication succeeds, so database failures silently disable limit enforcement.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`, `Authenticate` only fails authentication when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`; for any other `TagDevice` error it logs `"Failed to tag anonymous session"` and still returns an anonymous identity. Since `TagDevice` can now return persistence/counting errors from the DB-backed store (e.g., `CountDevices` error or `Exec` error in `CreateOrUpdateDevice`/`updateDevice`), those failures will effectively make the `device_limit` unenforced while anonymous auth continues. This is a real fail-open behavioral concern introduced by the change, though it’s not strictly “silent” because it is logged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97 — anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` on GrafanaBootConfig is inferred as type `undefined` while the GrafanaConfig interface declares `number | undefined`, and the constructor's `merge(this, defaults, options)` actually overwrites it with a real server-provided number at runtime, so the concrete class's static type is unsound relative to its own runtime contract.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` added to `GrafanaBootConfig` while `GrafanaConfig` declares `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined;`. From the diff alone, it's not verifiable that this class field is inferred as the *literal* type `undefined` (TypeScript commonly widens `undefined` initializers), nor is the referenced `merge(this, defaults, options)` constructor behavior shown in the provided diff hunk. Additionally, even if the field were typed as `undefined`, it is still assignable to `number | undefined` for the `implements` check, so the claimed “unsound relative to its runtime contract” cannot be confirmed from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Authenticate() now calls TagDevice synchronously on every anonymous request (was fire-and-forget in a goroutine), so every anon page load blocks on a DB round trip (and a COUNT query when device limit is set) instead of returning immediately

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Authenticate() changed from spawning a goroutine with a background context+timeout (fire-and-forget) to calling a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) inline and only then returning the identity (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go). TagDevice ultimately writes to the anon store; with the new device limit logic, CreateOrUpdateDevice() performs CountDevices() when s.deviceLimit > 0 before deciding to update vs upsert (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go). This makes anonymous request handling potentially wait on DB work (and an extra COUNT query when enabled). That’s a concrete, diff-grounded performance/latency concern, but not a clearly verifiable correctness defect since it may be intentional to enforce ErrDeviceLimitReached handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Removing the goroutine's dedicated 2-minute timeout context means TagDevice now runs under the caller's request context, so a slow/contended DB directly increases latency (or causes failures) for every anonymous authentication request, with no isolation from the auth request path

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Anonymous.Authenticate` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` changed from spawning a goroutine with `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)` around `anonDeviceService.TagDevice(...)` to calling `TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously on the auth path, and it now can return an error (e.g., `ErrDeviceLimitReached`) directly from authentication. This removes the previous isolation/timeout behavior and can couple anonymous auth latency/failure to DB contention or slow tagging work. That’s a concrete behavioral/performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff, but not an objectively verifiable correctness defect on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — TagDevice now runs synchronously on the request's own ctx with no bounded timeout, so a slow/hung DB blocks every anonymous authentication request instead of the previous fire-and-forget goroutine with a 2-minute timeout that degraded gracefully.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go removes the previous fire-and-forget goroutine that wrapped TagDevice in context.WithTimeout(..., 2*time.Minute) and instead calls a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously on the request path. There is no explicit timeout anymore in this code, so if the passed-in ctx has no deadline, a slow/hung TagDevice (which can hit the DB via anonStore) could block anonymous authentication requests. This is a concrete behavioral/performance/regression concern grounded in the diff, though whether it’s a correctness “bug” depends on external expectations for ctx deadlines and intended semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Removing the goroutine's defer recover() means a panic inside TagDevice/tagDeviceUI/CreateOrUpdateDevice now propagates directly out of Authenticate(), risking a crashed/500'd request instead of being safely logged and swallowed as before.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the goroutine wrapper and its `defer`/`recover()` in `Anonymous.Authenticate()` and replaces it with an inline `TagDevice(ctx, ...)` call. This means any panic occurring inside `TagDevice`/`tagDeviceUI`/store methods would no longer be caught at this boundary and could propagate up the auth/request call stack. However, whether that results in a crashed process or a 500 depends on higher-level HTTP panic recovery (not shown in this diff), and the diff does not demonstrate that these called methods actually panic. So the concern is real and diff-grounded as a resilience/behavior change, but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:74 — CreateOrUpdateDevice/updateDevice issue DB calls using the caller-supplied ctx with no per-call timeout applied anywhere in the anon store, so if the underlying DB stalls the query can block for as long as the (possibly unbounded) upstream context allows, whereas before it was capped at 2 minutes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous 2-minute deadline around tagging anonymous devices: in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go the goroutine + context.WithTimeout(..., 2*time.Minute) wrapper was deleted, and TagDevice is now called synchronously with the passed-in ctx. The anon store methods (CreateOrUpdateDevice/updateDevice) use the caller ctx directly via sqlStore.WithDbSession(ctx, ...) and do not apply any per-call timeout, so a stalled DB can now block as long as the upstream ctx permits (potentially unbounded), whereas previously the TagDevice DB work inherited the 2-minute timeout context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Anonymous.Authenticate now hard-fails authentication with ErrDeviceLimitReached, which is trivially triggerable by any client sending arbitrary, unsigned X-Grafana-Device-Id header values to exhaust the device cap and deny anonymous access to legitimate users (DoS via unauthenticated request)
matched_golden_ids: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core regression: Anonymous.Authenticate now fails when anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, preventing anonymous authentication once the device limit is reached (candidate additionally notes this can be abused for DoS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:124 — Device identity used for the new limit/enforcement logic (X-Grafana-Device-Id) is entirely client-supplied and unvalidated/unsigned, so the device count/limit mechanism can be trivially inflated or bypassed by spoofing arbitrary device IDs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a device-limit check in `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` based on `Device.DeviceID`, but it does not show where `DeviceID` originates (e.g., from the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header) nor any parsing/validation logic. The finding’s claim that the ID is “entirely client-supplied and unvalidated/unsigned” and thus trivially spoofable cannot be verified from the shown changes; the referenced header/identity source is not present in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:198 — AnonymousDeviceLimit is exposed to unauthenticated users via public frontend settings, giving an attacker the exact threshold needed to efficiently exhaust the device cap and trigger the anonymous-auth DoS

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds `AnonymousDeviceLimit` to `FrontendSettingsDTO` (`pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go`) and populates it in `getFrontendSettings` (`pkg/api/frontendsettings.go`), which means the value is sent to the frontend. However, the claim that this is exposed specifically to *unauthenticated* users and enables an anonymous-auth DoS cannot be fully verified from the diff alone (the access control/public-ness of the frontend settings endpoint isn’t shown). This is still a concrete, diff-grounded security/architecture concern about leaking an operational limit to clients, but not a definitively provable defect based only on the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51 — The only limit test stops at the store, so it misses that a failed over-limit tag remains cached and the same device is accepted on retry.

adjudication.rationale: The new limit behavior is only tested at the store layer (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit calls AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice directly). In this diff, the error is now propagated up the stack (AnonDeviceService.TagDevice now `return err` on UI tagging failure, and client.Authenticate returns early only when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`). There is also a local cache in AnonDeviceService (`localcache.New(...)`) with a dedicated safety test, but no test exercises the interaction between `deviceLimit`/`ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the service/client layers (including any cache effects on retries). The claim that an over-limit failure is cached and then accepted on retry is not directly verifiable from the shown code, but the missing higher-level test coverage for this new behavior is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:62 — The sequential test misses the non-atomic count-then-insert race that lets concurrent first-time devices exceed the configured cap.

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` the device limit check is implemented as a non-atomic `CountDevices(...)` followed by an insert/update (the upsert logic later in the function). There is no transaction/lock spanning the count+write, so two concurrent first-time devices can both observe `count < s.deviceLimit` and both proceed to insert, exceeding the cap. The added test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` is sequential and cannot detect this race, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:69 — The test never verifies that an existing active device can still be refreshed at capacity, leaving the new update-only success branch untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new “at capacity, update-only” logic in `CreateOrUpdateDevice`: when `count >= s.deviceLimit`, it calls `s.updateDevice(ctx, device)` instead of inserting. The new test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only covers the failure path (second, different `DeviceID` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`) and never exercises the success case where an existing, still-active device is refreshed/updated while at capacity (i.e., `UPDATE ... WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ...` affects 1 row). That leaves the intended update-only success branch untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Authenticate() changed from async fire-and-forget to synchronous with ErrDeviceLimitReached now failing anonymous auth, but there is no client_test.go at all exercising Authenticate, so this behavioral change has zero test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a clear behavior change in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go: Authenticate() no longer tags the device in a background goroutine with its own timeout, but instead calls TagDevice synchronously and returns an error when errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached). While new integration tests were added for the store/device-limit behavior (database_test.go) and TagDevice (impl_test.go), the diff adds no tests covering the Authenticate() path or the new "fail auth on device limit" behavior. However, the specific claim that "there is no client_test.go at all" cannot be verified from this diff alone.
